transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Miles Ortega (Redwood GTM), Tom Alvarez (Horizon Head of ML), Simone Park (CTO), Riley Chen (Director, Security), Asha Kapoor (VP Product)

Summary (auto): Quick co-sell triage across Horizon portfolio. Focus: which accounts to prioritize, which model variants to offer (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security gating for PHI, pricing expectations, legal procurement path.

Topics: pipeline mapping, joint demo owners, security/compliance gating, pilot SLOs, next-steps and dates.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see the Horizon crew. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll run a fast co-sell sprint today, Priya will cover technical gaps and Miles will surface co-sell motions.
[00:14] Tom Alvarez: Hey Jordan, thanks. Quick note, we've got a couple execs on the line but mostly product and security. Short on time so appreciate the structure.
[00:23] Priya Patel: Hi all, Priya here, SE. We'll try to give crisp answers and capture any blockers you have.
[00:30] Simone Park: Hi folks.
[00:33] Miles Ortega: Miles, Redwood GTM, focusing on partnership ops.
[00:36] Riley Chen: Riley, security. We mostly care about PHI handling and audit trails.
[00:40] Asha Kapoor: Asha, product. We'll try to prioritize top use-cases for the pilot.
[00:44] Jordan Kim: Ok, kickoff, two quick objectives: one, map your top six opportunities to co-sell plays; two, surface any security or procurement blockers. We'll end with owners and dates.

[02:10] Tom Alvarez: On the opportunities, rough list — clinical summarization, triage routing, patient messaging generation, claims pre-fill, provider search ranking, and a research assistant internal tool. The first three are high priority.
[02:45] Priya Patel: Great, on our side we typically categorize those by latency sensitivity and data residency. Summarization and messaging are tolerant to slightly higher latency but must keep PHI inside the VPC or on dedicated.
[03:20] Simone Park: So, we need to understand tradeoff — hosted API convenience vs private deployment for PHI. Can you outline where Redwood Recommend each?
[03:32] Jordan Kim: Sure, high level: hosted API is fastest to prototype and cheapest for non-PHI, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation for sensitive workloads, Private on-prem/VPC is for regulated workloads with strict KMS/HSM and audit requirements.
[03:50] Tom Alvarez: Is there a clear pricing delta we should expect between Dedicated and Private? Our procurement will ask.
[03:58] Miles Ortega: Typically Dedicated is reserved capacity subscription; Private includes licensing and support overhead. We'll send a pricing band but for co-sell we'd aim to structure incentive rebates for the first 6-12 months to offset up-front adoption costs.

[06:05] Riley Chen: From security side — SOC 2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs are mandatory. Also need clarification on what telemetry leaves the environment during hosted tests.
[06:22] Priya Patel: Good Q. For hosted we do collect usage metrics but we can restrict PII/PHI in logs; for pilot we recommend sandbox dedicated nodes or private so nothing leaves your VPC. We'll attach our security brief. Note — sometimes the transcript auto-cap says "Red-wood dedicate" but the product is Redwood Dedicated.
[07:10] Asha Kapoor: Ok, for the pilot success criteria — we need 95th pctl latency under 400ms for messaging, cost per 1k tokens under X (we'll share target), and quality floor on rouge/accuracy for summarization.
[07:30] Jordan Kim: Makes sense. Priya — can you run a quickbench with Horizon's sample dataset? We'll simulate both hosted and dedicated to show cost delta and latency tail.
[07:38] Priya Patel: Yep, I'll run a 48 hour sim with 95th/99th pctl metrics and different batch sizes. I'll try quantized model variants as well to show cost lift.

[09:00] Tom Alvarez: On the co-sell motion — who owns the initial outreach to the internal buyer? We want to avoid duplication and confusing messaging.
[09:10] Miles Ortega: Good call — we'll propose a playbook: Redwood AE coordinates with Horizon commercial lead, Redwood SE runs a joint demo, and a partner GTM rep (that's me) manages the channel credit and co-marketing. We'll share a one-pager for each account.
[09:40] Jordan Kim: We'll also add a shared pipeline spreadsheet with recommended lead owner, priority, ask, and quick win vs long-term. Link will be in the follow-up.

[11:50] Simone Park: A question on model variants — do you have recommended quantization or kernel tuning for healthcare models? We run some custom LLMs on top of our embeddings.
[12:05] Priya Patel: We do. For Bloom-style and GPT-like models we choose INT8 quant for cost savings, but we keep KV cache strategies to preserve context. There's also a compilation/kernels thing where certain GPUs get better tail latency. We'll list hardware recs — A100s vs H100 etc. Note: sometimes our docs confuse H100 and A100 names in auto transcripts.

[14:40] Riley Chen: Legal / procurement question — do you require data processing agreements and standard BAAs for PHI?
[14:50] Jordan Kim: Yes, BAAs are standard for PHI scenarios. For Private deployments we can do customer-managed keys with HSM integrations. Miles will facilitate legal intro.

[16:30] Asha Kapoor: For go-to-market messaging, we'd like to co-brand the case studies but need to vet wording carefully around PHI. Also need compliance sign-off.
[16:42] Miles Ortega: Totally — the marketing play will be tippy to 'hypothetical results' until legal signs off. We'll coordinate with your comms team.

[18:05] Tom Alvarez: On risks — big one is procurement timeline for private infra. If procurement pushes 60+ days that's going to kill velocity. Is there a way to do a hybrid pilot?
[18:20] Priya Patel: Hybrid is exactly our recommended path: start with hosted or dedicated sandbox to validate quality, then move to VPC/private once legal clears. We can also provision dedicated pools with tenant isolation while legal is in flight.

[20:10] Jordan Kim: Let's triage the top 6 accounts now — we'll call them A->F. Quick notes: A (Large payer) — high security, high ACV, needs private; B (Regional provider chain) — medium latency, open to dedicated; C (Digital-first clinic) — speed > latency, hosted ok; D (Clinical research) — needs audit logs, dedicated/private; E (Claims provider) — throughput sensitive, Dedicated; F (Internal research) — non-PHI, hosted ok.
[21:05] Simone Park: Agree. B and E look like best near-term co-sell wins because procurement is faster and decision owners are product/ops.
[21:18] Jordan Kim: Great, so priority list: B, E, C, A, D, F. We'll populate the mapping sheet.

[23:40] Tom Alvarez: Could you summarize the commercial ask for each? We need a simple one-liner for our internal folks.
[23:50] Miles Ortega: Yes. For B — reserved capacity pilot 3 months, for E — dedicated throughput trial, for C — hosted POC. We'll put pricing bands as ranges.

[26:00] Priya Patel: Quick technical add — for provider search ranking we recommend a reranker + embedding pipeline and suggest caching the top-k to reduce token cost. That sometimes gets mis-spelled as K V cache in notes.
[26:30] Asha Kapoor: Good. Also, do you support function-calling and structured outputs for our triage workflows? We rely on downstream systems.
[26:40] Priya Patel: Yes, streaming + function-calling is supported. We'll demo a structured output flow in the joint demo.

[29:00] Riley Chen: On auditability, how granular are your logs — token-level, request-level? And retention windows?
[29:12] Jordan Kim: Request-level metadata, with optional token-level traces if you opt-in for debug. Retention windows are configurable; for Private you control retention. We'll share the security pack with retention tables.

[31:45] Tom Alvarez: Any special compliance gap we should flag? If you already have SOC 2, ISO, and BAAs that covers a lot, but our internal risk team will look for penetration testing and formal pen-test reports.
[32:00] Riley Chen: Also zero-trust network connectivity and SAML/SSO for RBAC.
[32:10] Priya Patel: We do SAML and OIDC, RBAC, and can show audit logs. Pen-test reports are available on request; some are redacted. We'll add that to the doc pack.

[34:20] Jordan Kim: Ok, time for concrete owners and dates. Jordan — I'll own playbook send, Miles will intro legal, Priya owns bench, Asha to give POC criteria, Riley to send security answers.
[34:38] Asha Kapoor: Will do, I can compile the three priority use-cases by Monday.
[34:45] Riley Chen: I'll run through the security questionnaire and flag any SOC 2 gaps by next week.

[37:02] Tom Alvarez: For the exec alignment on 3/24 — what should be on the agenda? We want a short 20-30 minute meeting.
[37:10] Miles Ortega: Agenda: 1) Quick alignment on priority accounts and ask; 2) Pilot SLOs and timelines; 3) Legal/Proc next steps; 4) Marketing/co-branding guardrails. That should fit 25 minutes.

[39:50] Priya Patel: Small technical caveat — when we benchmark we need a sample payload and expected concurrency. Tom, can you share anonymized sample payloads and expected QPS?
[40:02] Tom Alvarez: Yes, we'll share a sanitized sample set, about 10k records, and expected concurrency is 20-50 QPS for messaging peak.

[42:30] Simone Park: Budget question — are there partner incentives for early adoption? If we commit to a 12-month reserved for some accounts, can we get price protection?
[42:45] Miles Ortega: Yes, we can discuss co-sell rebate and price protection for reserved capacity. We'll put options in the spreadsheet.

[45:05] Jordan Kim: Quick objection we often hear — "we already have infra and an internal MLOps team" — how do we position Redwood?
[45:15] Miles Ortega: We'll emphasize we remove serving complexity, manage tail latency, and provide a unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private so your infra team can focus on model improvements rather than ops.

[47:30] Tom Alvarez: One more technical — can Redwood handle differential privacy or redaction at inference time for logs?
[47:42] Priya Patel: We can redact sensitive fields and apply DP transforms pre-tokenization if you want. That usually goes into pre-processing on your side, but we can assist in pattern matching redaction.

[50:00] Asha Kapoor: Marketing note — we'll need a short customer-ready value prop for each co-sell play. Prefer 1-2 sentences and 3 bullets.
[50:08] Miles Ortega: We'll draft those.

[52:20] Jordan Kim: Any blocker that would kill a near-term pilot?
[52:25] Riley Chen: Biggest is legal/BAA not signed. If that stalls then we can't process PHI on hosted environments. But we can do non-PHI hosted proofs.

[53:00] Tom Alvarez: What about a quick privacy safe demo that uses synthetic data to show capability while legal completes?
[53:08] Priya Patel: Yes we do that all the time. We'll prepare a synthetic data demo for 3/17.

[55:40] Jordan Kim: Recap of action items and owners: Jordan send playbook + sheet; Priya run bench and synthetic demo; Miles intro legal; Asha provide POC criteria; Riley security questionnaire. Dates on action items in the follow-up.

[57:00] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. Any additional asks from Redwood?
[57:06] Jordan Kim: Just the sample payload and concurrency. And exec calendar for 3/24 if that works.

[58:10] Asha Kapoor: 3/24 works. We'll confirm time.

[59:15] Priya Patel: I'll attach the list of recommended infra and expected tail latency per GPU type in the follow-up.

[60:30] Miles Ortega: I'll drop the co-sell incentives options and draft a one-pager for each priority account.

[61:10] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone — we'll send follow-up with links to the playbook, mapping sheet (https://redwood.app/sheets/co-sell-mapping-74219), security pack, and proposed exec agenda.
[61:30] Tom Alvarez: Thanks all.
[61:34] Simone Park: Thanks.
[61:36] Riley Chen: Bye.

--- End of transcript ---
